conciseDefinition: Combinational digital circuit performing integer arithmetic and bitwise logic operations while emitting status flags.
technicalContext: Core computation unit inside core-execution-units driven by ALUOp signals from the Control Unit.

conciseDefinition: Expected memory latency combining cache hit time, miss rate, and lower-level miss penalty.
technicalContext: Used to evaluate multi-level L1/L2/L3 cache hierarchies quantitatively.

conciseDefinition: Analytical bound showing overall parallel speedup is limited by the non-parallelizable serial fraction of a program.
technicalContext: Explains diminishing returns when scaling thread counts across multi-core dies.

conciseDefinition: Upper stacked copper and dielectric interconnect layers fabricated atop active silicon transistors.
technicalContext: Routes signal buses, H-tree clock networks, and power distribution grids inside pkg-silicon-die.

conciseDefinition: Front-end hardware mechanism that guesses conditional branch direction and target before EXECUTE resolves flags.
technicalContext: Minimizes pipeline flush stalls on loops and conditional branches.

conciseDefinition: Shared set of parallel signal conductors carrying addresses, data words, or control assertions between units.
technicalContext: Separated logically into Address, Data, and Control buses inside the core.

conciseDefinition: Area-array flip-chip solder bumps connecting the active silicon die face directly to the package substrate.
technicalContext: Reduces parasitic inductance and IR voltage drop compared with perimeter wire-bonding.

conciseDefinition: Hardware guarantee ensuring multiple cores with private caches observe a consistent view of shared memory locations.
technicalContext: Implemented via snooping or directory protocols (e.g., MESI) across the on-die interconnect.

conciseDefinition: Memory lookup that finds the requested address tag valid inside the queried cache level.
technicalContext: Avoids costly traversal down to L3 or off-die DRAM.

conciseDefinition: Fixed-size contiguous block of memory bytes transferred as a single unit between cache levels and DRAM.
technicalContext: Exploits spatial locality when programs access consecutive addresses.

conciseDefinition: ISA design philosophy supporting multi-step instructions, variable instruction lengths, and memory-operand arithmetic.
technicalContext: Modern CISC CPUs decode variable instructions internally into fixed micro-operations.

conciseDefinition: Spatial arrival-time difference of a clock edge between two sequential flip-flops on a die.
technicalContext: Minimized using balanced H-tree clock networks because skew shrinks usable clock period.

conciseDefinition: Transistor circuit family pairing PMOS pull-up and NMOS pull-down devices for low static power.
technicalContext: Foundation of modern digital microprocessors and SRAM caches.

conciseDefinition: Stateless digital circuits whose outputs depend solely on present input values after gate delay.
technicalContext: Includes gates, multiplexers, decoders, and adders between clocked flip-flop barriers.

conciseDefinition: Binary and multi-bit command wires generated by the Control Unit to steer datapath multiplexers and latches.
technicalContext: Examples include RegWrite, MemRead, MemWrite, IRWrite, and ALUOp.

conciseDefinition: Average number of clock cycles required to complete one instruction.
technicalContext: TIAN-ISA v1 uses deterministic sequential CPI = 6; pipelined CPUs target CPI <= 1.

conciseDefinition: Pipeline dependency where an instruction needs a register result not yet written back by an earlier instruction.
technicalContext: Resolved in pipelined hardware by forwarding/bypass paths or stall bubbles.

conciseDefinition: Interconnected collection of registers, multiplexers, buses, and execution units carrying operands and results.
technicalContext: Steered every cycle by control signals from core-control-unit.

conciseDefinition: Combinational logic extracting opcode, register indices, and immediate constants from the Instruction Register.
technicalContext: Drives Control Unit decoding during stage 2 (DECODE).

conciseDefinition: High-density capacitor-based main system memory requiring periodic refresh cycles.
technicalContext: Accessed off-die through die-memory-controller and mem-main-interface.

conciseDefinition: Runtime power-management technique adjusting core supply voltage V_DD and clock rate f together.
technicalContext: Exploits V_DD^2 dynamic power scaling to keep silicon within thermal limits.

conciseDefinition: Initial wafer fabrication stages forming active transistor channels, gates, and source/drain junctions.
technicalContext: Resides directly on the crystalline silicon surface of pkg-silicon-die.

conciseDefinition: 3D multi-gate MOSFET where the conducting channel rises as a thin silicon fin wrapped by the gate electrode.
technicalContext: Improves electrostatic gate control and curbs short-channel leakage.

term: ALU Status Flags (Z, N, C, V)
conciseDefinition: Single-bit condition indicators capturing Zero, Negative, Carry, and Signed Overflow outcomes from ALU operations.
technicalContext: Evaluated by conditional branch instructions such as JZ and JNZ.

conciseDefinition: Bistable sequential storage cell that samples input D at a rising clock edge and holds Q steady for the cycle.
technicalContext: Forms architectural registers, counters, and FSM state memory.

conciseDefinition: Link-level unit of packetized traffic transmitted across an on-die Network-on-Chip router link.
technicalContext: Carries cache-line data or coherence messages over die-interconnect.

conciseDefinition: Combinational circuit adding two input bits plus carry-in to produce a sum bit and carry-out.
technicalContext: Cascaded or accelerated with carry-lookahead logic inside core-alu.

conciseDefinition: Computer organization separating instruction storage and bus pathways from data storage and bus pathways.
technicalContext: Adopted at L1 (L1i / L1d) in modern Modified Harvard CPUs and in TIAN-ISA v1.

conciseDefinition: Symmetric fractal wiring geometry delivering equal path lengths from a central clock source to distributed endpoints.
technicalContext: Minimizes clock arrival skew across multi-core dies.

conciseDefinition: Nickel-plated copper lid atop the CPU package spreading die heat flux and shielding fragile silicon.
technicalContext: Couples to the die through TIM and mates with an external heatsink.

conciseDefinition: On-die hardware controller translating cache-line miss requests into external DRAM timing commands.
technicalContext: Located along die perimeter for short routing through substrate to socket pins.

conciseDefinition: Average number of instructions retired per clock cycle (reciprocal of CPI).
technicalContext: Key microarchitectural efficiency metric in the Iron Law of Performance.

conciseDefinition: Dedicated internal register latching the fetched instruction during FETCH so decode and execution remain stable.
technicalContext: Holds the active instruction string/opcode across the 6-stage cycle.

conciseDefinition: Abstract hardware/software contract defining programmer-visible instructions, registers, memory model, and flags.
technicalContext: Decouples compiled software from underlying microarchitectural implementation.

conciseDefinition: Smallest, fastest core-private SRAM cache split into instruction (L1i) and data (L1d) arrays.
technicalContext: Feeds instruction fetch and load/store ports simultaneously without structural stalls.

conciseDefinition: Large on-die SRAM cache shared across cores to absorb L2 misses and track inter-core coherence.
technicalContext: Organized in slices distributed along die-interconnect.

conciseDefinition: CPU package contact grid featuring flat gold-plated pads on the substrate underside mating with socket spring pins.
technicalContext: Delivers power, reference clock, DRAM channels, and PCIe I/O lanes.

conciseDefinition: Core execution subsystem executing memory reads and writes while checking bounds and latching MAR/MDR.
technicalContext: Active during MEMORY_ACCESS for LOAD [addr]/LOADM and STORE instructions.

conciseDefinition: Internal interface register holding the target Data Memory address during a memory read or write.
technicalContext: Latches address 0..255 inside TIAN-ISA v1 MEMORY_ACCESS stage.

conciseDefinition: Bidirectional buffer register holding the data word read from or written to Data Memory.
technicalContext: Pairs with MAR to decouple core timing from memory bus handshakes.

conciseDefinition: Combinational selector routing one of several data inputs to a single output based on select control bits.
technicalContext: Selects ALU operands, write-back sources, and next PC value.

conciseDefinition: Packet-switched router fabric connecting processor cores, cache slices, and I/O controllers on one silicon die.
technicalContext: Replaces saturated shared buses in multi-core processors.

conciseDefinition: Dedicated register holding the index or address of the instruction currently being fetched.
technicalContext: Increments by +1 per instruction unless redirected by JMP, JZ, or JNZ.

conciseDefinition: Overlapped assembly-line execution of multiple instructions occupying sequential hardware stages concurrently.
technicalContext: Improves throughput (IPC) while single-instruction latency stays bounded by total stages.

conciseDefinition: Multi-ported ultra-fast SRAM/flip-flop bank at Tier 0 of the memory hierarchy holding GPRs.
technicalContext: Supports parallel dual-read (OpA, OpB) and single write-back per cycle.

conciseDefinition: ISA philosophy emphasizing simple, uniform, load-store instructions that streamline decoding and pipelining.
technicalContext: Arithmetic operates solely on registers while explicit LOAD/STORE access memory.

conciseDefinition: Cross-coupled 6-transistor latch memory retaining data without refresh as long as power is supplied.
technicalContext: Used for on-die L1, L2, and L3 caches due to single-digit nanosecond speed.

conciseDefinition: Throughput limitation caused by instructions and data competing over a single shared memory bus.
technicalContext: Mitigated in modern CPUs via split L1 caches and deep cache hierarchies.
